A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ELM research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original WMDP and Harry Potter evaluations, component ablations, probing, adversarial attacks, and training-progression results.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations and analyses, including additional baseline comparisons, a full-fine-tuning ablation, and adversarial and relearning results.

M1.justification: ELM retains its probability-ratio target, three training objectives, synthetic fluency training, and early-layer LoRA updates. Introspective classification reframes the perspective already present in v1 Section 3.2. Full fine-tuning is an added experimental control, not a replacement method.

E1.justification: Both versions use WMDP-bio/cyber, Harry Potter, MMLU, MT-Bench, and the same qualitative prompt domains and training corpora. The added attacks and fine-tuning comparisons test different procedures within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds RMU and RepNoise comparisons for Mistral-7B, Llama3-8B, and Llama3-8B-Instruct. v1 includes these comparators only for Zephyr-7B, leaving the other model blocks with original-model and ELM rows. Harry Potter comparator membership is retained.

E3.justification: The established metrics, judges, generation limit, and GCG settings are retained. v2 adds targeted experimental conditions for unconstrained layer fine-tuning, BEAST prompting, and autoregressive relearning on forget data, alongside settings for the new baseline runs. Detailed budgets for the new attacks are unspecified.

E4.justification: New Appendix E/Table 4 directly tests whether the low-rank constraint protects specificity. New Appendix H adds an illustrative BEAST attack and a fine-tuning attack testing knowledge recovery. These substantially extend the design and robustness analyses; the earlier loss-component, specificity, probing, and checkpoint analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its experimental results. Tables and plots continue to present point estimates; the additional hyperparameter sweeps do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing entries in Tables 1–3 are retained, while v2 adds six baseline rows and Table 4's full-fine-tuning results, including MMLU 45.2 versus LoRA 56.6. Appendix H newly reports retraining recovery from 29.7% to 42.2% Bio accuracy and 27.2% to 29.4% Cyber accuracy. Figure 4 also revises MMLU heatmap entries, including rank 4, eta=1000, from 0.01 to 0.03.

T1.justification: The Bayesian target-distribution derivation, transformer equations, and LoRA formulation are mathematically retained. v2 separately numbers an autoregressive factorization already written inline in v1 and expands its explanation, without adding substantive assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 presents the three-criterion evaluation framework as the central contribution motivating ELM. v2 centers introspective classification and newly asserts in its conclusion that effective concept unlearning requires model-guided distribution modification. This substantially redefines the claimed conceptual contribution, while retaining the headline empirical scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets unconstrained fine-tuning as causing broader knowledge damage and acknowledges that fine-tuning can restore erased knowledge, while claiming recovery is harder. Section 6 newly suggests overly aggressive probability modification as a cause of incoherence. Adjacent-concept degradation and conceptual interdependence remain limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds model-specific RMU and RepNoise hyperparameter grids, selected settings, selection criteria, and steering-coefficient information for the additional comparisons. Core ELM settings and the reported code, model, and data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Emulator and DeRa to contextualize probability-ratio modification, plus the BEAST citation. Its introduction more explicitly contrasts ELM with retraining, gradient reversal, and representation manipulation. Most related-work coverage and existing comparisons with prior unlearning methods are retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, classification explanation, method narrative, limitations, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. The narrative shifts toward introspective classification, the desiderata descriptions are compressed, and retained appendices are relettered around the new sections.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from single-column to two-column layout, with widespread resizing and relocation of figures, tables, and example boxes. Table 1 expands its comparator blocks, Table 4 is added, and captions and Figure 3's panel separation are revised.

improvement.justification: v2 fills gaps in comparisons across models and directly tests the low-rank design, strengthening support for existing claims. Its relearning result also exposes a robustness boundary. These gains are limited by sparse reporting of the new attack settings and claims not fully reconciled with the evidence: despite continued general fluency-superiority language, Table 1 reports Llama3-8B-Instruct R-PPL of 3.0 for RMU versus 7.4 for ELM.
